business_summary.text: Meesho is an Indian e-commerce platform focusing on marketplace services for small businesses and consumers, supported by its proprietary logistics network Valmo and AI-driven order processing.

call_points.text: No EBITDA guidance; LTM free cash flow is the guiding line and should improve quarterly.
The 4% Q4 contribution margin is the baseline; the 145 bps one-time logistics headwind is behind.
call_points.versus_prior: reiterates the 4.0% Q4FY26 contribution margin in memory

call_points.text: Contribution margin gains from here will be slower than the Q3-to-Q4 step, from ads and some fulfilment margin restoration.
Valmo in-sourcing has no target share; at around 50% the cost structure was most optimized.
Sort-centre automation is planned across the Valmo network over the next few years; capex model not decided.
Meesho Mall contribution margin is below the core marketplace and stays in an investment phase for the next few years.
Cash from operations was pressed as negative for three quarters; the CFO cited past one-offs and offered a reconciliation.
Management sees high inflation as a potential tailwind for value-focused players, with an offsetting risk to absolute spend.

penalties.authority: Assessment Unit of the Income Tax Department
penalties.details: Based on the said Assessment Order under Section 143(3) of the Income-tax Act, 1961 along with a Demand Notice under Section 156 of the Income-tax Act, 1961 for the Assessment Year 2023-24, the Assessment Unit of Income Tax Department has raised a tax demand aggregating to ₹14,99,73,82,840 (Rupees One Thousand Four Hundred Ninety Nine Crore Seventy Three Lakh Eighty Two Thousand Eight Hundred Forty only), including applicable interest.
penalties.impact: The Company is currently evaluating the Assessment Order and does not concur with the observations and adjustments made in the Assessment Order. The Company believes that it has adequate legal and factual grounds to contest the same and is taking necessary steps to protect its interest. Please note that a similar demand order was issued for the previous Assessment Year as well (i.e., 2022-23), which was duly disclosed in detail in the prospectus filed by the Company dated December 5, 2025 (please refer pages 558 and 559 of the prospectus in this regard). As indicated therein, the High Court of Karnataka, by an order dated April 17, 2025, granted an interim stay on such demand notice and the matter is currently pending. The Assessment Order along with the Demand Notice does not have any major adverse impact on the Company's financial position, operations, or other activities

exceptions: fine or penalty: Commissioner (Appeals), CGST – Thane Commissionerate, Mumbai (Order-in-Appeal passed under Section 107(11) of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 (CGST Act), in relation to )

penalties.details: Order-in-Appeal passed under Section 107(11) of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 (CGST Act), in relation to the applicability of Tax Collected at Source (TCS) under Section 52 on transactions between reseller and end customer for the period October 1, 2018, to March 31, 2020. Pursuant to the said order, the Appellate Authority has upheld the tax demand of approximately ₹14.29 crore, along with applicable interest and penalty under Section 74 of the CGST Act. The penalty imposed under Section 122 of the CGST Act has been set aside.
penalties.impact: Based on the Company’s detailed assessment, independent professional advice and legal position, the Company is firmly of the view that the demand raised under the said Order is unsustainable and without merit. Accordingly, the Company believes it has strong legal and factual grounds to challenge the Order. The Company remains highly confident of a favourable outcome in this matter. It may be noted that this matter has been previously disclosed in the prospectus filed by the Company dated December 5, 2025 (please refer to page 40). The Order has no material adverse impact on the Company's financial position, operations, business or any other activities.

operating_notes.text: The company received an Order-in-Appeal upholding a tax demand of ₹14.29 crore relating to TCS on reseller transactions for October 2018 to March 2020.
FY26 NMV ₹41,560 Cr (+39% YoY); Q4FY26 NMV ₹11,371 Cr (+43% YoY), with normalized Q4 growth at 39% adjusting for the earlier Meesho Blockbuster Sale.
FY26 growth spends (indirect A&SP) rose 103% YoY to ₹990 Cr, or 2.4% of NMV versus 1.6% in FY25.
Prepaid orders reached c.34% of shipped orders in Q4FY26; Meesho Mall NMV grew ~82% YoY and Content Commerce NMV 105% YoY in Q4FY26.
Q4FY26 NMV reached ₹11,371 Cr (+43% YoY) and FY26 NMV reached ₹41,560 Cr.
Q4FY26: Meesho utilised ₹267.26 Cr of its ₹4,100.49 Cr net IPO proceeds, leaving ₹3,833.23 Cr unutilised and parked in bank fixed deposits and current accounts.
Q4FY26 contribution margin was 4%, which management set as the baseline after a 145 bps one-time logistics headwind in Q2 and Q3 FY26.
Valmo in-sourcing was around 50% of volumes, with no target share; sort-centre automation is planned over the next few years.
FY26 NMV to GMV ratio was 58.8%, within the 58-60% range of the last three years; more than two-thirds of sellers by GMV are active on ads.
Over 75% of orders on Meesho originate from AI-driven personalised feeds powered by its proprietary PRISM intelligence system.
Valmo accounted for about 50% of volumes in Q1FY27, similar to the previous quarter.
Close to two-thirds of GMV-contributing sellers advertise on the platform, with ROAS similar to the previous quarter.
For more than 50% of GMV-contributing sellers, Meesho is a primary source of income, per internal surveys.
Sudhir Ganesh Sitapati appointed as Additional Non-Executive Independent Director for 5 years from Oct 28, 2026.
Additional investment of up to USD 100,000 approved for Meesho Networks LLC (USA).
Income tax demand of ₹1,499.74 Cr for AY 2023-24 and ₹572.07 Cr for AY 2022-23 are being contested.
Annual Transacting Sellers grew 60% YoY to 1.13 million.
GPU footprint increased by 150% to support AI workloads ahead of festive season.
Engineering productivity rose 171% between March and September 2026 due to AI agent adoption.
MPPL (Lending Service Provider) turnover grew from ₹2.36 Cr in FY25 to ₹11.05 Cr in FY26.
Retail Pulse Labs (RPLPL) turnover grew from ₹4.92 Cr in FY25 to ₹16.04 Cr in FY26.

timeline.summary: Meesho received an Order-in-Appeal from the Commissioner (Appeals), CGST Thane Commissionerate upholding a tax demand of ₹14.29 crore.
Meesho reported Q4FY26 NMV of ₹11,371 Cr (+43% YoY) and FY26 NMV of ₹41,560 Cr (+39%), with FY26 loss of ₹1,358 Cr and cash of ₹6,750 Cr.
Meesho reported Q4FY26 NMV of ₹11,371 Cr (+43% YoY) and FY26 NMV of ₹41,560 Cr, with contribution margins recovering to 4.0%.
On May 6, 2026, Meesho Limited uploaded its Key Performance Indicators on its investor website pursuant to SEBI regulations.
Meesho filed its monitoring agency report for Q4 FY26, showing ₹3,375.27 Cr of IPO proceeds utilized during the quarter.
Meesho Limited shared the Q4 FY 2025-26 earnings conference call recording on May 6, 2026, via its website.

On 12 May 2026, Meesho filed the transcript of its 6 May 2026 Q4FY26 earnings call, where management set the 4% Q4 contribution margin as the baseline, gave no EBITDA guidance, and said the FY26 logistics headwind was one-time.
Meesho released an update on the adoption and scale of its proprietary AI system PRISM, powering over 75% of orders.
Q2FY27 results (consolidated): revenue ₹4,131.58 Cr, net loss to shareholders ₹132.45 Cr.
Meesho reported Q2FY27 NMV growth of 23% YoY to ₹12,911 Cr and expanded its contribution margin to 6.0%.
Meesho released the Monitoring Agency Report for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, showing ₹2,080.86 Cr in unutilised IPO proceeds.
Meesho board approved a ₹400 Cr investment in its lending arm MPPL and further investments in Kirana Club and Retail Pulse Labs.
Meesho Limited shared the Q2 FY 2026-27 earnings conference call recording on October 28, 2026, via its website.
